soundness_flags.label: ass:bounded-hazards
soundness_flags.one_line: A known common ceiling L for every arm and cause is a substantive restriction, not the standard continuous-time separable-effects condition supported by MartinussenStensrud2023; retag it novel and state how L is externally justified or calibrated.

soundness_flags.label: ass:bounded-hazards
soundness_flags.one_line: The proposal supplies no realistic basis for a researcher knowing one valid common hazard ceiling, although the active-ceiling frontier and mesh claim load-bearingly depend on it.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article formulates exchangeability, consistency, positivity, and dismissible-component conditions, identifies the continuous-time g-functional, and states that it imposes no structure on P for its efficient-influence-function result; it does not make a known common uniform hazard ceiling part of the standard separable-effects condition.

The paper distinguishes four-arm identification from two-arm identification and states that additional assumptions, including dismissible component conditions and strong positivity, are needed in the two-arm setting.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Retag the known common ceiling as novel, give an external scientific or administrative route for setting L, and add a sensitivity corollary quantifying how endpoints change when L is replaced by a conservative Lbar.

For the finite-switch OEQ, retain the handle but add one fully specified positive-cell two-cycle instance and state the exact constrained-Hessian or pulse-exchange predicate whose sign would certify compression versus obstruction.
Strengthen the mesh theorem into a design corollary that minimizes worst-case width over grids of fixed K, including the uniform-grid optimum and an explicit clinically interpretable width target.

recommended_next_step: Revise the hazard-ceiling assumption into an honestly novel, justified sensitivity/model restriction, then continue this same field-tier frontier angle.
